div.p: SAVE THESE IMPORTANT SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS

Powerwall 3 installation and service require knowledge of high voltage electricity and should only be performed by Tesla Certified Installers. Tesla assumes no liability for injury or property damage due to repairs attempted by unqualified individuals or a failure to properly follow these instructions. These warnings and cautions must be followed when using Powerwall 3.
indicates a hazardous situation which, if not avoided, could result in injury or death.
indicates a hazardous situation which, if not avoided, could result in minor injury or damage to the equipment.
indicates an important step or tip that leads to best results, but is not safety or damage related.

Read this entire document before installing or using Powerwall 3. Failure to do so or to follow any of the instructions or warnings in this document can result in electrical shock, serious injury, or death, or can damage Powerwall 3, potentially rendering it inoperable.

Electric shock hazard. The DC conductors of any connected PV system are normally ungrounded but will become intermittently grounded without indication when the inverter measures the PV array isolation. Disconnect all sources of supply before servicing.
A battery can present a risk of electrical shock, fire, or explosion from vented gases. Observe proper precautions.

This product can expose you to chemicals including cobalt and lithium compounds known to the State of California to cause cancer and birth defects or other reproductive harm. For more information, visit www.P65Warnings.ca.gov. Only members of the Tesla Service team and Tesla-certified technicians should open the external casing.
Powerwall 3 installation must be carried out only by Tesla Certified Installers trained in dealing with high voltage electricity.
Powerwall 3 is heavy. Use of lift equipment is recommended.
Use Powerwall 3 only as directed.
Do not use Powerwall 3 if it is defective, appears cracked, broken, or otherwise damaged, or fails to operate.
Before beginning the wiring portion of the installation, ensure that Powerwall 3 is switched off, and open any associated circuit breakers and disconnect switches.

Do not attempt to open, disassemble, repair, tamper with, or modify Powerwall 3. Powerwall 3 and its components are not user serviceable. Batteries in Powerwall are not replaceable. Contact Tesla Support or the Certified Installer who installed the system for any repairs.

When transporting Powerwall 3, handle with care. Do not impact, pull, drag, or step on Powerwall 3. Do not subject Powerwall 3 to any strong force. Leave Powerwall 3 in its shipping packaging until it is ready to be installed.
Do not insert foreign objects into any part of Powerwall 3.
Do not expose Powerwall 3 or its components to direct flame.
Do not install Powerwall 3 near heating equipment.
Do not immerse Powerwall 3 or its components in water or other fluids.
Powerwall is not designed nor warrantied for non-stationary applications.
Risk of electric shock. Do not remove cover, there are no user serviceable parts inside. Refer servicing to qualified personnel.
Both AC and DC voltage sources may be terminated inside this equipment. Each circuit must be individually disconnected before servicing.
When the PV array is exposed to light, it supplies a DC voltage to this equipment.
Do not use cleaning solvents to clean Powerwall 3, or expose Powerwall 3 to flammable or harsh chemicals or vapors.
Do not use fluids, parts, or accessories other than those specified in this manual, including non-genuine Tesla parts or accessories not purchased directly from Tesla or a Tesla-certified party.
Do not place Powerwall 3 in a storage condition for more than one month, or permit the electrical feed to be severed for more than one month. Contact your installer for more information if needed.
Do not paint any part of Powerwall 3, including any internal or external components such as the exterior shell or casing.
When installing Powerwall 3 in a garage or near vehicles, keep it out of the driving path. If possible, install Powerwall 3 on a side wall and/or above the height of vehicle bumpers.
Install Powerwall 3 in a location that prevents damage from flooding.
Operating or storing Powerwall 3 in temperatures outside its specified range might cause damage to Powerwall.
Ensure that no water sources are above or near Powerwall 3, including downspouts, sprinklers, or faucets.
Ensure that snow does not accumulate around Powerwall 3.

section.p: This device complies with part 15 of the FCC Rules. Operation is subject to the following two conditions: (1) this device may not cause harmful interference, and (2) this device must accept any interference received, including interference that may cause undesired operation.

This device has been tested and meets applicable limits for Radio Frequency (RF) exposure. This equipment should be installed and operated with minimum distance 20 cm between the radiator and your body.

This device contains licence-exempt transmitter(s)/receiver(s) that comply with Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada’s licence-exempt RSS(s). Operation is subject to the following two conditions: (1) this device may not cause interference, and (2) this device must accept any interference, including interference that may cause undesired operation of the device.
The device for operation in the band 5150–5250 MHz is only for indoor use to reduce the potential for harmful interference to co-channel mobile satellite systems.

div.p: Tesla Powerwall 3 comes with a warranty whose term depends on the connection of Powerwall 3 to the Internet.

To secure the full 10-year warranty for Powerwall 3, it must be reliably connected to the Internet to allow remote firmware upgrades from Tesla. If an Internet connection is not established or is interrupted for an extended period, and Tesla is unable to contact you, the warranty may be limited to 4 years.
For more information, refer to the Tesla Powerwall Warranty for your region at tesla.com/support/energy/powerwall/documents.

div.p: Care and cleaning instructions for Powerwall 3.

section.p: Powerwall 3 is capable of charging and discharging within the operating temperature range specified below. At the extremes of the temperature range, Powerwall 3 may limit charge or discharge power to improve battery lifespan.

1Powerwall 3 is designed to operate in all climates and in direct sunlight, from temperatures of -20°C to 50°C (-4°F to 122°F). Performance may be de-rated at operating temperatures above 40°C (104°F).
Keep the immediate area around Powerwall 3 clear of foreign objects and debris to maintain optimal airflow.

div.p: Do not lean on, stack anything on top of, or hang anything from Powerwall 3 or from wires or conduit leading to Powerwall 3.
To clean Powerwall 3, use a soft, lint-free cloth. If needed, the cloth can be dampened with mild soap and water only.
Do not use cleaning solvents to clean Powerwall 3 or expose Powerwall 3 to flammable or harsh chemicals or vapors.

section.p: Powerwall 3 does not require pre-scheduled preventative maintenance. The only maintenance required by an owner is to keep the Powerwall unit free and clear of debris, especially around the air intake and exhaust.

div.title: Powerwall 3 Owner's Manual

div.p: Powerwall 3 is a fully integrated solar and battery system that stores energy from solar production. It converts energy from solar panels or Solar Roof, and its rechargeable battery pack provides energy storage for solar self-consumption, load shifting, or off-grid use. Powerwall 3 is installed with Backup Switch, Backup Gateway 2, or Gateway 3 to control the system's connection to the grid and monitor home energy consumption.

section.p: A Powerwall 3 system for whole home backup is designed to store energy from the grid or solar, and power the entire home during a grid outage.

p.strong: Whole Home Backup with Backup Switch

section.p: A Powerwall 3 system for partial home backup is designed to store energy from the grid or solar, and can power some home loads during a grid outage. These loads are selected during the system design phase, and the installer configures the system at installation to exclude all other loads from backup.

div.p: Tables of components and part numbers.

td.p: Powerwall 3 is an integrated solar and battery system that converts energy from solar panels or Solar Roof to be used by the home, and stores excess energy for future use.
Powerwall is installed with one of the following Tesla devices.
The Backup Gateway 2 is installed in partial and whole home backup systems.
Powerwall controls operation of the system, while Backup Gateway 2 monitors energy usage and manages the transition to and from backup operation.
The Gateway 3 is installed in whole home backup systems.
Powerwall controls operation of the system, while Gateway 3 monitors energy usage and manages the transition to and from backup operation.
The Tesla Backup Switch is only installed in whole home backup systems.
Powerwall controls operation of the system, while Backup Switch monitors energy usage and manages the transition to and from backup operation.

div.p: Components and features of the Powerwall 3 unit.

The On/Off Switch and optional System Shutdown Switch both act as Rapid Shutdown (RSD) initiators. These switches are used by emergency responders to trigger rapid shutdown of the solar array in the event of an emergency.

div.p: This is a landing page for several subtopics about system operations and troubleshooting.

Powerwall systems provide control and monitoring capability through the Tesla app. During normal operation, Powerwall 3 communicates with Backup Gateway 2, Gateway 3, or Backup Switch, and the Powerwall 3 On/Off switch should remain in the ON position. When troubleshooting Powerwall 3 operation, it may be necessary to turn off Powerwall 3 or refer to its LED indicator to confirm that it is operating properly.
Do not operate Powerwall 3 unless all covers are in place.
Do not disconnect anything from or add anything to Powerwall 3.
Do not try to communicate with Powerwall 3 using third party tools or diagnostics between Powerwall and the Backup Gateway 2, Gateway 3, or Backup Switch.
Monitor Powerwall 3 system operation from your mobile device using the Tesla app.

section.p: The Tesla app allows you to monitor the following from your mobile device:

ul.li: Relative amounts of energy used from solar, grid, and Powerwall storage

li.span: Download the latest version of the Tesla app from tesla.com/support/tesla-app.
Open the Tesla app on your mobile device and sign in to your Tesla account.
Select your Powerwall system from the home screen to view system operation.
li.div: The app displays real-time power usage, energy consumption history, and relative amounts of energy used from solar, grid, and Powerwall storage.

div.p: Diagnose and resolve issues with Powerwall 3 backup operation.

li.span: If a brownout or blackout is experienced during backup operation, reduce the loads and check that the load breakers have not opened.

div.p: See tesla.com/support/energy/powerwall/own/best-practices-during-power-outages for best practices to extend the backup duration of your system during an outage.

li.span: If it is necessary to restart the Backup Gateway 2, Gateway 3, or Backup Switch, press the Reset button on the device when directed to do so by Tesla Support.

div.p: The Reset button and manual override switch are located on the Backup Gateway 2, Gateway 3, or Backup Switch. The Backup Switch conduit hub must be removed to access the Reset button or manual override switch.

tr.td: Backup Gateway 2 / Gateway 3 / Backup Switch RESET button
Backup Gateway 2 / Backup Switch manual override switch
Backup Gateway 2 / Gateway 3 circuit breaker (in most whole-home backup systems)

div.p: To remove the Backup Switch conduit hub, use a Phillips PH2 screwdriver to loosen the three captured fasteners holding it in place, then remove the hub. Once service actions are complete, replace the conduit hub and tighten the three fasteners.

li.span: If it is necessary to manually reconnect to the grid, operate the manual override switch on the Backup Gateway 2 or Backup Switch when directed to do so by Tesla Support.

div.p: Improper operation of the manual override switch may damage the unit and could void the product warranty. Do not remove the conduit hub or operate the manual override switch unless directed to do so by Tesla Support, or in the event that the grid is present but you are experiencing an outage. Contact Tesla Support if you are not sure whether you should operate the manual override switch.
Do not make any modifications or adjustments to the Utility Meter. Only interact with the Backup Switch.

li.span: Push the Backup Switch manual override switch in to manually connect the system to the grid.
To check the Backup Switch LED status, remove the conduit hub as described above and locate the LED near the Reset button.

section.p: If the issue persists after completing these steps, contact Tesla Support at tesla.com/support/energy/more/additional-support/contact-us.

div.p: If Powerwall 3 is unresponsive, it may be necessary to turn off or power cycle the system. Note that power cycling the system must be done in the proper sequence as defined below.

section.div: Warning: On Powerwall 3 systems with additional interconnected solar, always turn off the solar inverter(s) or disconnect the solar source(s) before turning off Powerwall 3.

li.span: Turn off Powerwall 3 by setting its On/Off switch to the OFF position.
Turn off the AC breaker to Powerwall 3.
Turn off the AC breaker to the Gateway, if installed (for whole-home backup systems, this may be a breaker inside the Gateway).
Wait for at least one hour.
Turn the AC breakers back on.
Turn on Powerwall 3.

div.p: If the system is not working correctly, perform the following steps.
div.div: CAUTION: Powerwall 3 , Backup Gateway 2, Gateway 3, and Backup Switch are not user-serviceable and must be repaired by Tesla or a Certified Installer.
Warning: Do not open the deadfront cover inside the Gateway. Exposed wiring can present a risk of electrical shock.
div.p: Check the LED indicator on Powerwall 3 to determine its status:

tr.td: Powerwall 3 is idle. Will enter sleep state if no actions in progress
Powerwall 3 is off or in sleep state

div.p: If it is not possible to communicate with the system through the Tesla app, ensure that the home Internet connection is working. If the home Internet connection is working and communication through the Tesla app is still not possible, see tesla.com/support/energy/powerwall/mobile-app/connecting-powerwall-wi-fi for instructions to update your Wi-Fi connection.

h1.span: What to Do in Case of an Emergency

div.p: Steps to take in the event of a fire, flooding, unusual smell or smoke, or unusual noises from Powerwall 3.

section.p: In the event of any threat to health or safety, always complete the following two steps before addressing the scenario-specific steps below:

ol.li: Immediately contact the fire department or other relevant emergency response team.
Notify all people who might be affected and ensure that they can evacuate the area.

div.p: Only perform the suggested actions below if it is safe to do so.

li.span: On Powerwall 3 systems with additional interconnected solar, turn off the AC breaker for all solar inverters.
Turn off all Powerwall(s), then turn off the AC breaker to Powerwall(s).
Turn off the Powerwall 3 integrated DC isolator.
Turn off the AC breaker to the Gateway, if installed.
If using a fire extinguisher, use only water, CO2, or ABC type extinguishers.

div.p: Do not use type D (flammable metal) extinguishers.

li.span: Stay out of the water if any part of the battery, Gateway, or wiring is submerged.
On Powerwall 3 systems with additional interconnected solar, turn off the AC breaker for all solar inverters.
Turn off all Powerwall(s), then turn off the AC breaker to Powerwall(s).
Turn off the Powerwall 3 integrated DC isolator.
Turn off the AC breaker to the Gateway, if installed.
If possible, find and stop the source of the water and pump water away from the system.
If any part of the unit was submerged, note the depth and duration of the flooding.
Contact Tesla Support to determine if the unit can be safely turned back on.
If Tesla Support confirms it is safe to turn the unit back on, allow the area to dry completely before use.
On Powerwall 3 systems with additional interconnected solar, turn off the AC breaker for all solar inverters.
Turn off all Powerwall(s), then turn off the AC breaker to Powerwall(s).
Turn off the Powerwall 3 integrated DC isolator.
Turn off the AC breaker to the Gateway, if installed.
Ensure nothing is in contact with Powerwall.
Ventilate the room.
Turn off all Powerwall(s), then turn off the AC breaker to Powerwall(s).
Turn off the Powerwall 3 integrated DC isolator.
Turn off the AC breaker to the Gateway, if installed.
Ensure that nothing is blocking the air intake or exhaust vents on the Powerwall or in the fan.

section.p: In all cases, once the situation is stable, contact the Tesla Certified Installer who installed the system.
For first responder information, see tesla.com/firstresponders.
